why: Bible Atlas places this Carmel in the hills of Judah. Amos 1:2 pairs it with the shepherds' meadows as a mountain whose summit withers, and most readers take it to be the coastal Mount Carmel, so that mountain is linked in its place.
In 1:11 'Edom' and 'his brother' mean the nation of Edom, so the patriarch Esau is not meant here.
Bible Atlas puts Kir at Kir-hareseth in Moab. Amos 1:5 means the Aramean Kir to which Damascus's people go into exile, whose location is unknown, so no dot is drawn.
'Syria' is a generic point in northern Syria. Amos 1:3-5 names Damascus and its nearby places, which are mapped separately.
Amos 1:8 names the Philistines and 1:13 names the Ammonites; Bible Atlas does not link these peoples' lands in this chapter.
In 2:1 'Moab' is the nation, whose land is already linked as a place, and the 'Edom' of 2:1 is the nation too. The patriarch Esau and the person Moab are not meant here.
'Israel' in 2:6-11 means the northern kingdom and its people, not the patriarch Jacob/Israel whom Bible Atlas links.
'Israel' in 3:1, 3:12 and 3:14 means the people or the northern kingdom, not the patriarch.
'Israel' in 4:5 and 4:12 means the people, not the patriarch.
Bible Atlas puts this Gilgal on the coastal plain. Amos pairs Gilgal with Bethel as a worship site (4:4), and most scholars look for it near the Jordan or in the hill country, so the dot is omitted.
Bible Atlas puts this Gilgal on the coastal plain. Amos pairs Gilgal with Bethel as a worship site (5:5), and most scholars look for it near the Jordan or in the hill country, so the dot is omitted.
'The house of Joseph' and 'the remnant of Joseph' (5:6, 5:15) mean the northern tribes and kingdom, not the patriarch Joseph.
Bible Atlas places Calneh in southern Iraq. Amos 6:2 names it with Hamath and Gath, which points to Calneh in northern Syria, so the dot is omitted.
Bible Atlas gives this 'Arabah' the same point as Hamath, which is wrong. The 'wadi of the Arabah' in 6:14 is the southern limit of the kingdom, in the rift valley south of the Dead Sea.
'Joseph' in 6:6 stands for the northern kingdom (the 'ruin of Joseph'), and 'Israel' in 6:1 and 6:14 means the nation; neither means the patriarch. David in 6:5 is the king, so that link stays.

'Israel' in the chapter means the northern kingdom and its people, not the patriarch. 'The high places of Isaac' and 'the house of Isaac' (7:9, 7:16) are poetic names for the same people, not the patriarch himself.
'Israel' in 8:2 means the people. 'Dan' in 8:14 is the sacred site where a calf shrine stood (a place), not the son of Jacob.
Bible Atlas places this Carmel in the hills of Judah. Amos 9:3 means the coastal Mount Carmel, a high place with caves and dense cover, so that mountain is linked in its place.
Bible Atlas puts Kir at Kir-hareseth in Moab. Amos 9:7 means the Aramean Kir, whose location is unknown, so no dot is drawn.
9:7 names the Cushites and the Philistines, whom Bible Atlas does not link in this chapter.

'Israel' means the people, 'Esau' in the chapter's Edom reference means the nation, and 'the fallen booth of David' (9:11) is read as David's dynasty or kingdom (some Christians and Jews read it as a messianic promise). The person David and the patriarchs are not named.
The Hebrew word 'Harmon' (4:3) is obscure, and its place is unknown; the translation and the Bible Atlas point are guesses, so no dot is drawn.
